ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, in parallelogram $ABCD$, $AC$ and $BD$ intersect at point $O$, and $E$ is the midpoint of $AB$. If $OE = 6$, what is the length of $AD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since quadrilateral ABCD is a parallelogram, \\
it follows that $BO=DO$, \\
since point E is the midpoint of AB, \\
it follows that $OE$ is the median line of $\triangle ABD$, \\
hence $AD=2OE$, \\
since $OE=6$, \\
it follows that $AD=\boxed{12}$

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A and B form the bottom side of the parallelogram, D is above A, C is above/right of B, diagonal BD crosses diagonal AC at O, and E lies on segment AB with segment EO drawn to O. From the text, ABCD is a parallelogram, AC and BD intersect at O, E is the midpoint of AB, and OE=6. Use the fact that diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other, so O is the midpoint of BD. In triangle ABD, E is the midpoint of AB and O is the midpoint of BD, so EO is a midsegment parallel to AD and has half its length. Therefore AD=2·OE=12.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the parallelogram has adjacent side vectors from A to B and from A to D, with E halfway along AB and O at the crossing of the diagonals. From the text, ABCD is a parallelogram, E is the midpoint of AB, and O is the intersection of the diagonals. Use a vector/coordinate setup: place A at the origin, let B be vector b and D be vector d, so C=b+d. Since E is the midpoint of AB, E=b/2. The diagonal intersection O is the midpoint of BD, so O=(b+d)/2. Then vector EO=O−E=(b+d)/2−b/2=d/2. Thus OE=|d|/2=AD/2. Given OE=6, AD=12.
